This order is passed in continuation of order dated 18.01.2022, which read as under:
"1.

By this petition, the petitioner seeks regular bail in FIR No. 199/2009 under Sections 406/420/467/468/471/120B/174A IPC registered at P.S.EOW as also setting aside of the order dated 18th August 2021 of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, whereby, the bail application of the petitioner was dismissed.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner states that at page 5 of the status report, it is stated that the petitioner is involved in 13 ITRs, however, in RC No. 5/E/99 mentioned at serial No. 1, the petitioner has not been named as an accused nor summoned, liven in ITRs mentioned at serial Nos. 5, 6, 8 and 12, the petitioner has neither been named as an accused nor ever summoned.

He further states that in two FIRs mentioned at serial Nos. 4 and 7, the petitioner has been acquitted and in the remaining FIRs also, the petitioner has either settled the matter or making efforts to settle.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner further states that in the above-noted FIR, the allegations are against the petitioner, his brother and late father.

The petitioner was not initially arrested and on 30th July 2013, a MOU was entered into between the Saket Sharma vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137432697/
1 petitioner, his brother and the complainant by virtue of which, the petitioner was to pay a sum of Rs.66 lakhs to the complainant.

sentences.text: The petitioner paid a sum of Rs.20 lakhs, however, the balance amount of Rs.46 lakhs could not be paid and thus, the petitioner was arrested on 30 October 2013.

As the petitioner expressed his desire to settle the matter, after a few days of custody, the petitioner was granted interim bail but since he did not appear in the interregnum, he was declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 25th May 2016.
Learned counsel for the petitioner also states that in the meantime, in the year 2018, the balance amount as per the MoU was paid by the brother of the petitioner.

The complainant while opposing the bail application does not deny that the settled amount has been received by the complainant but only harping on the conduct of the petitioner involved in number of cases, that he was absconding, was declared proclaimed offender on 25th May 2016 and could be arrested only in the year 2020.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further states that during this period when the petitioner was declared proclaimed offender, amount had been paid by the petitioner's brother and the petitioner to the complainant and the petitioner had been personally appearing before different Courts.
Hence, the plea that the petitioner had absconded and the declaration on that count, is unwarranted and illegal.

4. The petitioner will file an additional affidavit, indicating the present status of all the 13 FIRs registered against the petitioner within one week with advance copy to the learned APP for the State, who will verify the same and file a detailed status report.

State will also verify whether the amount settled between the complainant and the petitioner and his brother on the other side has been duly paid or not and whether the petitioner has roots in the society so as to ensure his presence during the course of trial."
2. It is the submission of the learned senior counsel for the petitioner the affidavit in terms of order dated 18.01.2022 has since been filed.
I have perused the said affidavit dated 23.02.2022 wherein the status of 13 FIRs as alleged against the petitioner is mentioned.

If one peruse the said table we would find in FIRs mentioned at serial nos.1, 5, 7, 8 and 12 the petitioner has not been named as an accused; in FIRs mentioned at serial nos.3, 4, 6, 10 and 13 the accused is rather acquitted/ the FIR is either disposed of or the matter is settled.
It is only in FIRs mentioned at serial nos. 2, 9 and 11 the status is shown to be pending.

3. The order dated 18.01.2022 was passed in the presence of learned counsel for complainant as also the learned APP for the State, wherein it is recorded the entire payment of cheated amount has been made to the complainant.

The said order rather notes the complainant while opposing the bail of the present petitioner does not deny the amount received but was only harping upon the conduct of the petitioner being involved in number of cases and the petitioner was absconding and declared as a proclaimed offender on 25.05.2016 and was arrested only in the year 2020.
4. Be that as it may, now since 12.07.2021 the petitioner is arrested in the present FIR and has spent more than one year and five months.

Thus, considering the fact the cheated amount has since been Saket Sharma vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137432697/
2 paid to the complainant; the status of FIRs as per affidavit dated 23.02.2022; the period of custody of the petitioner and the investigation qua him being complete, there is no use to continue with the custody of the present applicant, hence in the circumstances, the petitioner herein is admitted to bail on his executing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with one surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court.

sentences.text: The petitioner shall furnish his contact/address details to the Investigating Officer/SHO concerned.
The petitioner is further directed not to contact/threaten/coerce the witnesses/complainant in any manner lest it shall be a ground for cancellation of his bail.
5. The petition stands disposed of along with pending application(s).
6. A copy of this order be communicated to the learned Trial Court/Jail Superintendent for information and compliance.
7. Order dasti.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
